components.html:
Open model probabilities, scoring, and evidence

Game scoring: 1,000 for any basket that clears all five hard rules, 0 for a blocked basket or timeout, plus up to 300 speed points. Agreement with Commerce-1 does not change the score.

Real precomputed output from the public Commerce-1 artifact on NVIDIA H200. The store and scenario are synthetic.

Open inference receipt

narrative.overview: Checkout Rush turns one bounded commerce decision into a short arcade mission. A lavender floor holds a single ink game console: receipt-like mission telemetry on top, Maya's fixed customer brief at left, and a paper start/choice/result deck at right. Bricolage Grotesque supplies the game-show urgency; DM Sans and IBM Plex Mono keep constraints, time, points, and model probability inspectable. The loop has three explicit states. Ready explains the mission and starts no clock. Playing exposes four candidate actions and a 15-second countdown. Result shows policy outcome and game points, then compares the player's action with Commerce-1's frozen Choice distribution. Commerce-1 remains sealed until the player commits or times out. The arcade layer is subordinate to product truth. Points reward only clearing five deterministic checkout rules and responding before the clock expires. Model agreement is displayed separately, never treated as correctness, and never changes the score. Synthetic scenario data and precomputed inference stay visible in the result evidence.
keyCharacteristics: One elevated console containing HUD, timer, brief, play deck, and result.
An explicit Start action before any time pressure begins.
Four full-row candidate buttons with A–D shortcuts.
Policy outcome and points as the game result; model agreement as comparison.
Violet action and clock motion, lime constraints, coral urgency/focus.
Full Choice probabilities, scoring rules, and provenance behind one disclosure.

rules.name: The Explicit Start Rule
rules.body: The clock never begins on page load; the player starts the mission deliberately.

rules.name: The Score Is Not the Model Rule
rules.body: Policy compliance and remaining time determine points. Commerce-1 agreement never changes them.

rules.name: The Model Stays Sealed Rule
rules.body: Do not reveal the model choice or probabilities before the player commits or times out.

rules.name: The Lavender Is Outside Rule
rules.body: Lavender surrounds the console; paper and ink own the game.

rules.name: The Signal Needs Language Rule
rules.body: Lime, coral, red, and green never carry time, match, pass, or block meaning without text or structure.

rules.name: The Violet Is Not Approval Rule
rules.body: Violet marks action, time, and model material—not safety or checkout authority.

rules.name: The Game Voice Leads Rule
rules.body: Use Bricolage for mission, prompt, quote, price, points, and result—not dense evidence.

rules.name: The Telemetry Uses Mono Rule
rules.body: Use IBM Plex Mono for bounded facts and controls, never narrative copy.

rules.name: The Brief Persists Rule
rules.body: The five hard constraints remain adjacent to every game state.

rules.name: The Safety Facts Survive Rule
rules.body: Mobile may hide nutrition detail, but never price, time, nut status, cart limit, or policy verdict.

rules.name: The HUD Is Game State Rule
rules.body: Mission, time, points, and status are the only top-level telemetry; model metrics live after commitment.

rules.name: The One Cabinet Rule
rules.body: Do not elevate rows, comparisons, policy slips, or HUD cells independently.

rules.name: The Soft Cabinet, Sharp Controls Rule
rules.body: Round the enclosing console and compact markers; keep actions, rows, comparison blocks, and policy slips square.

dos: Do preserve Ready → Playing → Result and start the clock only on explicit action.
Do keep score tied only to policy-safe eligibility and time remaining.
Do keep model choice/probability sealed until commit or timeout.
Do present policy verdict, game points, and model agreement as separate concepts.
Do preserve button semantics, A–D/S/Enter/R shortcuts, result focus, polite share feedback, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do retain price, prep time, nut status, cart limit, and checkout verdict at every width.
Do disclose synthetic scenario data, precomputed inference, scoring rules, and the public receipt.
donts: Don't award points for matching Commerce-1 or call a match correct.
Don't call 82.99% a game score, policy verdict, benchmark, explanation, or checkout authority.
Don't imply live inference, autonomous purchase, real-store facts, nutrition advice, or an allergy guarantee.
Don't expose model output before commitment or place model metrics in the ready HUD.
Don't detach result from brief, merge policy with probability, or hide the block reason.
Don't add retailer branding, food photography, gradients, glass, nested shadows, or dashboard analytics.
Don't hide the Open model link, inference receipt, project links, or core boundaries to save space.
